scope: Authored fictional meeting packs. The pilot pack expands the repository's existing synthetic preview. No real meeting notes are included.

packs.title: pilot readiness review
packs.question: What is blocking the pilot launch?

docs.title: Readiness notes
docs.text:
# Launch readiness

The accessibility review is open. Keyboard focus is lost when the invitation dialog closes. This blocks the pilot launch until the fix is verified.

# Rollback

A rollback owner has not been assigned. The rollback checklist requires restoring the previous invitation flow and checking that existing accounts still sign in.

# Decision date

The team will review readiness on Thursday. No launch date has been agreed. The proposed pilot is limited to an invited group of 25 participants.

# Support

Support will record invitation failures and login failures separately. Each report needs the browser version and the step where the problem occurred.

docs.title: Pilot acceptance checklist
docs.text:
# Accessibility gate

Before launch, verify keyboard navigation, visible focus and screen-reader labels in the invitation flow. The review is still open.

# Success measures

Measure invitation acceptance and successful first sign-in. A successful sign-in must reach the workspace, not just return a successful authentication response.

# Stop conditions

Pause invitations if an existing account loses access or the rollback process fails. Do not widen the pilot until the issue is understood.

# Follow-up

The product manager will bring the open checklist to the Thursday readiness review. An owner must be recorded for every unresolved gate.

packs.title: service incident review
packs.question: What caused the queue backlog and what should we fix?

docs.title: Incident timeline
docs.text:
# Initial alert

At 09:12 the processing queue began growing after a worker release. Request acceptance continued, but completed jobs fell below incoming jobs.

# Diagnosis

The release reduced the database connection timeout. Failed database calls retried immediately, increasing load and causing a retry storm.

# Mitigation

At 09:31 the team restored the previous timeout and reduced concurrent workers. The queue began draining at 09:38. No accepted jobs were deliberately discarded.

# Evidence gap

The timeline does not establish whether every customer job completed. Reconcile accepted job IDs against completion records before declaring full recovery.

docs.title: Remediation notes
docs.text:
# Retry policy

Add bounded exponential backoff with jitter to database retries. Cap the number of attempts and send exhausted jobs to a visible failure queue.

# Release checks

Load-test the timeout change with slow database responses. Compare completion rate, retry volume and database saturation before rollout.

# Monitoring

Alert on queue age as well as queue length. A small number of very old jobs can be hidden by a low total queue count.

# Ownership

The platform developer owns the retry change. The verifier must reproduce the slow-database case and check that retries remain bounded.

packs.title: market research review
packs.question: How will we check whether the strategy survives outside training?

docs.title: Research plan
docs.text:
# Hypothesis

Test whether a simple trend rule remains useful after turnover costs. The benchmark is passive exposure on the same dates, with the same price source.

# Walk-forward design

Choose the lookback only within each training window. Freeze that choice for the next test window. Concatenate only the test returns for the reported out-of-sample curve.

# Execution timing

A signal computed at the close cannot earn that day's return. Lag positions so the trade occurs after the information becomes available.

# Costs

Charge transaction costs when positions change. Report sensitivity to higher fees rather than a single frictionless result.

docs.title: Review questions
docs.text:
# Data audit

Check missing dates, duplicate bars, corporate actions and timezone alignment before interpreting returns. Record the source and retrieval date.

# Evaluation

Compare drawdown, turnover and return dispersion alongside average returns. Inspect each test window so one unusual period cannot hide the rest.

# Selection bias

Keep the search log, including failed parameter choices. A strong result chosen from many experiments needs a separate untouched evaluation period.

# Decision

No live allocation has been approved. The next deliverable is a reproducible notebook with assumptions, test windows and a failure-case review.

packs.title: engineering handoff
packs.question: What must the verifier check before release?

docs.title: Release scope
docs.text:
# Product change

The new import screen accepts CSV files and previews the first 20 rows before saving. Users map their column names to the required fields.

# Validation

Reject duplicate record IDs and missing required columns. Keep the original file unchanged. Show row-specific errors so the user can correct the source.

# Large files

The browser preview is limited to 5 MB. Larger files require the local importer. The page must explain the limit before a file is uploaded.

# Persistence

A failed import must not partially replace the existing dataset. Write to a temporary store and commit only after validation passes.

docs.title: Verifier checklist
docs.text:
# Functional checks

The verifier must test valid files, missing columns, duplicate IDs, empty input and a file above the size limit. Reopen a saved dataset and compare the row count.

# Interaction checks

Check keyboard access to the file chooser and mapping controls. Error messages must be associated with the relevant field.

# Recovery checks

Simulate a failed save. The previous dataset should remain readable, and retrying a corrected file should succeed.

# Release decision

The developer supplies the change and test receipts. The verifier records a pass or a specific blocking failure; a green build alone does not establish a working import flow.
